findings.title: Valid ticket links can fail the check
findings.description: `visibleText` removes HTML comments before removing code, so a literal `<!--` inside a fenced block or inline code span can hide a later, ordinary `Closes #20` line. When the code contains no matching `-->`, `closingIssueNumbers` sees no closing reference even though the reference is outside the code.

findings.title: A PR body can stall ticket checks
findings.description: `visibleText` applies a backreference regex with repeated matching attempts to an entire attacker-controlled line, so a long backtick run can cause extensive backtracking. The ticket-link workflow passes the PR body into this parser, allowing such input to consume the job's five-minute budget before it reports a result.

findings.title: PR bodies can exhaust issue lookups
findings.description: `run` performs a sequential authenticated lookup for every distinct closing reference without limiting how many it will ask for. A PR body with many `Closes #N` references, including one whose title names no ticket, can consume the job timeout or API allowance before the check decides whether the PR has paperwork to verify.

findings.title: A failed comment strands a ticket
findings.description: The Investigation guard removes `ready-for-agent` before posting its recovery comment, without handling failure of `gh issue comment`. If that request fails after label removal, the step stops before its explicit diagnostic, leaving the ticket unlabeled and without instructions to re-add the label.

findings.title: Script header and field docs describe the old check
findings.description: The header of `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` says the check runs from `.github/workflows/check.yml` and only covers PRs whose title names a ticket. The `PrTicketInput.title` doc says ticket ids are read "from here only", and `PrTicketResult.tickets` is described as the ids named in the title. In fact the check now runs from `ticket-link.yml`, and `ticketsOf` also collects tickets from closed issues whose titles start with `T-NNN:`. Someone who trusts these comments will look in the wrong workflow, and may think a PR without an id in its title is never checked, which is the old limit that finding 823561fb fixed.

findings.title: Code text can pass the ticket link check
findings.description: `visibleText` removes inline code with a regex that cannot cross a newline, leaving a backtick-delimited multiline code span intact. A PR body consisting of a backtick, then `Closes #20` on the next line, then a closing backtick makes `closingIssueNumbers` return issue 20 although the keyword is code rather than ordinary text.

findings.title: Script output bypasses the cli-only rule
findings.description: The entry blocks of `scripts/pr-ticket-check.ts` and `scripts/ticket-ready.ts` call `process.stdout.write`, `process.stderr.write` and set `process.exitCode`. The checklist allows these only in `src/cli.ts`, so the literal rule is breached in two files. The author reports that the human chose to amend the rule in AGENTS.md to allow entry blocks under `scripts/`, but the checklist text still forbids it, so the same wording will flag every factory script that follows the amended convention until the rule is re-imported.

findings.title: Any guard crash is reported as a missing investigation
findings.description: The guard step treats every non-zero exit of `node scripts/ticket-ready.ts` the same way: it removes the `ready-for-agent` label and posts a comment saying the ticket has no Investigation section. A script crash, a module that fails to load, or a Node problem on the runner therefore sends the human to edit a ticket that is fine, and the real error appears only in the job log.

review_agent_comment: Using GitHub’s closing-issue references is easier to trust than parsing the PR body by hand. Please mark the three check contexts as required in main’s branch protection; until then, quality gate point 9 is enforced only by convention.
